title: We will guard it
hook: We sent down the reminder and We will guard it (15:9)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ibrahim's prayer at the House. And a week ends: thunder praising, change from inside, hearts at rest, thanks that grows, a good word like a tree.

A new surah, al-Hijr, and it opens with an insult. Verse six, in paraphrase: they say, you, the one the Reminder is sent down to, you are surely mad. Why don't you bring us angels, if you're telling the truth? The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a man with a message and few people on his side. Three verses later comes the answer.

Verse nine, in paraphrase: it is We who sent down the Reminder, and it is We who will guard it. Listen to the Arabic pile up emphasis: inna nahnu, truly We, We ourselves, sent it; wa inna lahu la-hafizun, and truly, for it, We are guardians. Every part of the sentence says: this isn't on your shoulders. To a mocked man in Mecca, that's comfort before it's doctrine. The book's survival doesn't depend on whether the crowd believes him today. The Reminder, adh-dhikr, is one of the Qur'an's names for itself, the thing that brings to mind what people forget. Last year you met the huffaz, the memorizers, whose title comes from this verse's root. Muslim teachers point to the guarding at work through them, through the written copies gathered under Abu Bakr and 'Uthman, and through something smaller: how a copy is treated in an ordinary home. The written Qur'an is called the mushaf. Another surah says none touch it but the purified, and jurists drew a rule from it: handle the mushaf in a state of ritual purity, with wudu, though some read the verse differently. It's kept on a high shelf, above other books, never on the floor or under a pile. Some families wrap it in cloth. A worn-out copy isn't thrown away; it's buried in clean ground, or respectfully disposed of in other ways. None of that is the guarding the verse promises. God says He guards it. But people have answered that promise with their own small care.
screen: `YOU ARE MAD, THEY SAY.` · `TRULY WE, WE SENT IT; WE GUARD IT.` · `ADH-DHIKR — THE REMINDER.` · `THE MUSHAF: A HIGH SHELF, CLEAN HANDS.` · then, large: `IT IS GUARDED.`

segments.voice: If there's a copy of the Qur'an nearby, look at where it sits: high and clean, or under a pile of mail? If you'd like, give it an honored place; if you don't have one, think of a book or object that holds something precious for your family. If you pray, recite one short surah you know by heart.
Adh-dhikr. The Reminder, one of the Qur'an's names for itself: 15:9 says God sent it down and God will guard it. Today's word.
Your line: it is guarded. Not on your shoulders. Day four hundred forty-eight, and a week complete.

howItsDone: Muslims keep copies of the Qur'an on high shelves, often wrapped in cloth, and handle them after wudu; worn-out copies are buried or respectfully disposed of, never thrown away.

fork.reveal: it's buried, or respectfully disposed of; a mushaf is kept with care from its first day to its last.

original.note: Arabic: "surely guardians," the last word of 15:9, from h-f-z, the root of hafiz.

trapdoor: what you thought: God promises the book won't be lost.
what it means: a promise to a mocked Prophet that the message doesn't depend on him, answered by believers with their own care.
what a scholar hears: 15:9 stacks emphasis (inna, nahnu, inna, la-); it answers the taunt of 15:6–7; the purity rule for the mushaf rests mainly on 56:79 and is debated by a minority.

chat.says: What does it mean that God will guard the Qur'an?
options: 15:9 says God sent the Reminder and God guards it; people's care answers that.
It means only memorizers may hold a copy, so no one else can harm it.
It means the Qur'an needs no care at all, so how it's kept doesn't matter.
chat.meaning: Verse nine: it is We who sent down the Reminder, and We who guard it. People answer that promise with small care, like a high shelf.

adh-dhikr.meaning: the Reminder, a name the Qur'an gives itself

huffaz.meaning: those who know the Qur'an by heart

mushaf.meaning: a written copy of the Qur'an

sources.ref: Qur'an 56:77–79 (none touch it but the purified)

notes: 15:9 paraphrased; Pickthall's wording was not quoted because the exact word order wasn't certain.
